Hi Bonnie,

First off, I owe you a real apology. This reply took far too long, and that's not how we like to treat people who reach out. My sincere apologies for the wait.

Now, to your question: yes, in Central Texas you can absolutely still sow milkweed in summer. You're past the cool-spring window, but Texas heat is actually what most milkweed species thrive in, especially the ones native to your region.

For caliche soil, the species that will handle those dry, alkaline, rocky conditions best is Asclepias tuberosa (Butterfly milkweed). It takes poor, dry soil very well and is one of the most reliable bloomers. Asclepias fascicularis (Narrowleaf milkweed) is another drought-tolerant option worth trying in tough soil.

I'd steer you away from Asclepias syriaca (Common milkweed), it prefers looser, loamier soil and won't perform well in caliche.

For summer sowing in Texas, direct seeding works best: scratch the surface, press the seeds in lightly, water well at first, and let the heat do its thing. No cold stratification needed at this time of year.

You can find our seed packets here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/milkweed-seeds

Hope this helps you get some milkweed going despite that caliche.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
